 1          Pursuant to Civil L.R. 16-9, Plaintiff WEST COAST CONFERENCE, an unincorporated

 2   association (“Plaintiff” or the “WCC”), and Defendant GRAND CANYON UNIVERSITY, an

 3   Arizona nonprofit corporation (“Defendant” or “GCU”; collectively with Plaintiff, the “Parties”),

 4   respectfully submit this Joint Case Management Statement.

 5   1.     JURISDICTION AND SERVICE

 6          Jurisdiction is proper in this court under 28. U.S.C. § 1332 based on complete diversity of

 7   citizenship between the WCC and GCU and because the matter in controversy exceeds $75,000.

 8   Venue is proper in this Court pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) because a substantial part of the
 9   events or omissions giving rise to the claim occurred in this district. Additionally, the Parties
10   contractually agreed to venue in the United States District Court for the Northern District of
11   California. No issues exist regarding personal jurisdiction or venue.
12   2.     FACTS
13         1.      Plaintiff’s position: On or about May 9, 2024, the WCC and GCU entered into an
14   agreement (“Agreement”), pursuant to which GCU agreed to become a member of the WCC

15   according to the terms and conditions of the Agreement as well as the WCC’s Constitution. On

16   May 10, 2024, the conditions under the Agreement were met and the Agreement became

17   effective and is binding on the parties. The Agreement provides for GCU to make an Equity

18   Buy-In Payment to the WCC. As a courtesy to GCU, the Agreement allowed GCU to make

19   those payments on a schedule commencing in July, 2024 and concluding in January, 2031. The

20   first two payments were due before January 15, 2025. GCU did make the first payment, received

21   by the WCC on or about July 11, 2024. The Agreement and Constitution of the WCC have

22   certain Withdrawal Provisions, setting forth the parties’ obligations if GCU withdraws from the

23   WCC. Specifically, if GCU gives notice of a withdrawal that relates to a withdrawal by GCU for

24   a fiscal year ending on or before June 30, 2031, then GCU is obligated to make a one-time

25   payment to the WCC, not later than 30 days after its written notice of withdrawal, in an amount

26   equal to the remaining unpaid Equity Buy-In Payment. Further, if GCU does not give at least 12

27   months prior notice of its withdrawal, it is obligated to make a further one-time payment to the

28   WCC. The Agreement does not give GCU the unilateral right to withdraw from the WCC or to

                                                                             CASE NO.: 3:24-CV-08933-CRB
                                  JOINT STATUS CONFERENCE STATEMENT
             Case 3:24-cv-08933-CRB            Document 35        Filed 03/21/25      Page 3 of 9




 1   terminate the Agreement, either prior to or after July 1, 2025, without any further obligation to

 2   the WCC. On or about November 1, 2024, GCU publicly announced its decision to join and

 3   compete in the Mountain West Conference (“MWC”) beginning July 1, 2025 and provided a

 4   voicemail message to the WCC’s Commissioner. Also on November 1, 2024, GCU provided

 5   notice in writing that it was “terminat[ing]” the Agreement. GCU reiterated in writing on

 6   November 13, 2024 that it had terminated the Agreement, and stated that it would not compete in

 7   the WCC during the next school year (2025-2026). These communications from GCU to the

 8   WCC constituted a notice of its withdrawal from the WCC. GCU has joined a different
 9   conference, the MWC. GCU has breached its obligations under the Agreement by, among other
10   things, (a) failing and refusing to make the payments due under the Agreement and Constitution
11   and/or (b) by its statements and conduct, expressly and impliedly repudiating the Agreement and
12   refusing to make the Equity Buy-In Payment as it become due. The factual issues in this case
13   may include various issues related to GCU’s timing of its decision to join a different conference,
14   the financial incentives to do so, issues relating to the negotiation of the contract, including what
15   was included and what was excluded as terms, and the performance of the parties until GCU’s
16   decision to leave the WCC.
17         2.      Defendant’s position: The WCC is a collegiate athletics conference. GCU is a
18   university located in Arizona whose athletic programs currently compete in the Western Athletic

19   Conference. By letter dated May 9, 2024, the WCC “extend[ed] an invitation to [GCU] to join

20   the WCC as a full member effective July 1, 2025....” (the “Invitation”). The Invitation also

21   repeats in at least four other provisions that GCU’s prospective membership in the WCC would

22   not begin until July 1, 2025, and GCU would therefore not become subject to the WCC’s

23   Constitution, Bylaws and Administrative Regulations (the “Constitution”) until that date. The

24   Invitation also required GCU to make an “Initial Equity Buy-In” pursuant to the Constitution,

25   and further states that the WCC’s Presidents’ Council “determined” that GCU’s Initial Equity

26   Buy-In would be $18 million, payable over fourteen installments. The parties further agreed that

27   the first of these installments, in the amount of $1.5 million, would be due between July 1 and

28   15, 2024. Finally, the Invitation describes the consequences for any “failure” of GCU to make

                                                                              CASE NO.: 3:24-CV-08933-CRB
                                   JOINT STATUS CONFERENCE STATEMENT
               Case 3:24-cv-08933-CRB          Document 35         Filed 03/21/25      Page 4 of 9




 1   these installment payments, which differed depending on whether the non-payment occurred

 2   before or after GCU joined the WCC as a member. If such non-payment occurred prior to GCU

 3   becoming a member, the Invitation provides that the WCC could sanction GCU by revoking its

 4   acceptance into the conference “without any right of refund of prior payments....” If such non-

 5   payment occurred after GCU became a member, the Invitation provides that the WCC could

 6   sanction GCU by, among other things, suspending its member distributions and/or expelling

 7   GCU from the conference.

 8            On May 9, 2024, GCU’s President countersigned the Invitation and returned it to the
 9   WCC. Material to GCU’s decision to countersign the Invitation was the parties’ mutual belief
10   that Gonzaga University (“Gonzaga”) would continue to be a member of the WCC. On July 11,
11   2024, GCU paid the WCC the first installment payment of its Equity Buy-In in the amount of
12   $1.5 million. Subsequently, on or around October 1, 2024, it became publicly known that
13   Gonzaga intended to leave the WCC to begin competing in a different athletics conference.
14            By letter dated November 1, 2024, GCU informed the WCC that it sincerely appreciated
15   the invitation to join the conference but had “decided to respectfully decline the invitation at this
16   time” and was therefore “providing written notice that it hereby terminates the May 9, 2024,
17   letter Agreement....” On that same date, GCU also attempted to reach the WCC by phone and left
18   a voice message to similar effect. The WCC responded by putting out a press release and

19   initiating this lawsuit through a “Complaint for Damages” alleging one count for breach of

20   contract. This claim fails because, among other reasons, GCU committed no breach by refusing

21   to make withdrawal payments to a conference it had not yet joined and, in any event, the

22   amounts sought by the WCC represent an unenforceable penalty and/or an unlawful restraint of

23   trade.

24   3.       LEGAL ISSUES

25            Certain legal issues were addressed by the Parties in the Motion to Dismiss, and relate to

26   whether GCU is required to pay the unpaid amount of the remaining Equity Buy-In fee and the

27   exit fee as set forth in the contract and the WCC Constitution and based on the facts described by

28   the Parties in Section 2, supra., as developed in discovery, and as set forth in their filed papers and

                                                                              CASE NO.: 3:24-CV-08933-CRB
                                   JOINT STATUS CONFERENCE STATEMENT
             Case 3:24-cv-08933-CRB            Document 35        Filed 03/21/25      Page 5 of 9




 1   pleadings in this action. GCU has also raised various affirmative defenses relating to the

 2   announcement that Gonzaga University was leaving the WCC and the effect, if any, on the

 3   Agreement.

 4   4.     MOTIONS

 5          The above referenced Motion to Dismiss was denied by the Court on February 12, 2025.

 6   (ECF 30.) Both the WCC and GCU anticipate filing motions for summary judgment and/or

 7   motions for partial summary judgment.

 8   5.     AMENDMENT OF PLEADINGS
 9          1.      Plaintiff’s Position: Given the Court’s denial of the Motion to Dismiss and
10   Defendant’s filing of its Answer, Plaintiff does not intend to amend the Complaint at this time.

11          2.      Defendant’s Position: GCU requests that the time for amendment of the pleadings

12   remain up to and including August 1, 2025 to account for the possibility that discovery may reveal

13   facts regarding the WCC’s knowledge of Gonzaga’s departure from the conference that would

14   support additional affirmative defenses and/or a counterclaim.

15   6.     EVIDENCE PRESERVATION

16          The Parties in this matter are preserving evidence related to this action by, for example, not

17   destroying documents pursuant to a document destruction program and not deleting electronically

18   recorded material. The Parties discussed the fact that litigation hold letters were issued.

19   7.     DISCLOSURES

20          The Parties have agreed to exchange their initial disclosures on April 11, 2025.

21   8.     DISCOVERY

22          Although no discovery has been issued to date between the Parties, the Parties will

23   endeavor to explore the extent to which stipulations may be reached regarding facts and the

24   authenticity and admissibility of documents.

25          The Parties have not identified any special issues related to electronically-stored

26   information, privilege, phasing, etc., which need the Court’s attention. As such, no special orders

27   related to discovery are required from the Court.

28

                                                                             CASE NO.: 3:24-CV-08933-CRB
                                  JOINT STATUS CONFERENCE STATEMENT
             Case 3:24-cv-08933-CRB            Document 35        Filed 03/21/25     Page 6 of 9




 1          The Parties will further meet and confer regarding discovery and production of documents

 2   in this matter, and have exchanged the Court’s standard Stipulated Protective Order.

 3   9.     CLASS ACTIONS

 4          Not applicable.

 5   10.    RELATED CASES

 6          Not applicable.

 7   11.    RELIEF

 8          1.      Plaintiff’s Position: Plaintiff seeks damages in excess of $18.5 million, including
 9   the unpaid amount of the contractual Equity Buy-In Payment, the withdrawal payment obligation

10   pursuant to the contract and the WCC Constitution, and consequential damages resulting from the

11   breach of GCU’s payment obligation. Plaintiff also seeks prejudgment interest and recovery of its

12   reasonably incurred attorneys’ fees and costs pursuant to the contractual provision permitting

13   recovery of such fees and costs to the prevailing party. Defendant raises an issue regarding

14   whether Plaintiff properly pled its damages, but that issue was raised in the Motion to Dismiss,

15   and it was denied. Defendant’s attempt to re-argue this issue below is not allowed under the

16   Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

17          2.      Defendant’s Position: GCU seeks a defense judgment, and recovery of its

18   reasonably incurred attorneys’ fees and costs pursuant to the contractual provision permitting

19   recovery of such fees and costs to the prevailing party. As it relates to the scope of discovery, GCU

20   contends that the WCC’s Complaint does not include a prayer for the consequential damages that

21   the WCC now indicates, supra, it intends to seek. See Compl. (Dkt. No. 1) at p. 4 (“WHEREFORE,

22   WCC prays for judgment against GCU as follows ... For compensatory damages according to

23   proof....”) (emphasis supplied); see also Schasa v. AmTrust Bank, CV 11-01108-RGK, 2011 WL

24   13220099, at *3 (C.D. Cal. Aug. 2, 2011) (“There are two types of damages: (1) general, and (2)

25   special. General damages with respect to contract claims are often characterized as those that flow

26   directly from a breach … Special damages are those losses that do not arise directly from a breach,

27   but are secondary or derivative losses … Under both federal rules and California law, special

28   damages must be specifically pled.”)(emphasis supplied); Lewis Jorge Constr. Mgmt., Inc. v.

                                                                             CASE NO.: 3:24-CV-08933-CRB
                                  JOINT STATUS CONFERENCE STATEMENT
             Case 3:24-cv-08933-CRB            Document 35         Filed 03/21/25       Page 7 of 9




 1   Pomona Unified School Dist., 34 Cal. 4th 960, 968 (2004) (“Contractual damages are of two types

 2   – general damages (sometimes called direct damages) and special damages (sometimes called

 3   consequential damages).”). GCU also raised this argument as part of the briefing on its Motion to

 4   Dismiss. See Grand Canyon University’s Reply Memorandum of Points and Authorities in Support

 5   of Motion to Dismiss (Dkt. No. 27) at n.2 (“To the extent the WCC seeks some other unspecified

 6   form of relief, its Complaint fails to state a plausible claim for a different reason – it makes no

 7   effort to plead actual damages proximately caused by Grand Canyon’s purported breach.”).

 8   12.    SETTLEMENT AND ADR
 9          The Parties stipulate to participate in private mediation through the selection of a mutually
10   agreeable mediator.
11   13.    CONSENT TO MAGISTRATE JUDGE FOR ALL PURPOSES
12          Plaintiff has declined to consent to a magistrate judge.
13   14.    OTHER REFERENCES
14          At this time, the Parties do not believe that this action is an appropriate action to be referred
15   to binding arbitration, a special master, or the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation.
16   15.    NARROWING OF ISSUES
17          Although no party discovery has been taken to date, the Parties will endeavor to explore
18   the extent to which stipulations may be reached regarding facts and the authenticity of documents.

19   It is also anticipated that issues may be narrowed by summary judgment motion practice.

20   16.    EXPEDITED TRIAL PROCEDURE

21          The parties do not believe that this case is an appropriate case to be handled on an expedited

22   basis with streamlined procedures.

23   17.    SCHEDULING

24          Per the Court’s standing order, the Parties suggest the following dates for case
